fields.statement: QA at 30e69b6fe with a binary built from the branch (go build -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza), in a scratch Rhiza root and repo with fake rex and claude on PATH and a clean env. git config rhiza.daemon.permissionMode manual, then rhiza run start --workflow plan --autonomous with no --permission-mode: 'Queued a plan run ... for the daemon', and .git/rhiza/starts.json holds the start with no permission_mode key. rhiza daemon --max-runs 3 --once (no --permission-mode): 'Started a run of <cs>', the queue drained, and the run's journal records permission_mode "manual" and autonomous true; run ls shows it live at step interview. With the setting = nonsense the start is refused at queue time (claude-code: unknown permission mode "nonsense", exit 2) and nothing is queued. With the setting = bypassPermissions the start is refused by the dedicated-machine trust check (exit 1, nothing queued) exactly like an explicit --permission-mode bypassPermissions; after writing trust = "dedicated" to machine.toml the same start queues with no mode recorded, which is the incident's case.

QA at 30e69b6fe with a binary built from the branch, in a scratch Rhiza root and repo. With rhiza.daemon.permissionMode unset, rhiza run start --workflow plan (no --permission-mode) exits 2 with: step "interview" is an agent step with no permission mode: give --permission-mode, set rhiza.daemon.permissionMode (for a run the daemon starts), or set permission_mode on the step; .git/rhiza does not exist afterwards, so nothing was queued. With the setting = manual, rhiza run start --workflow plan --foreground exits 2 with the same message.
